mainTopic: Two people doing one מלאכה together: the מיעוטים of בַּעֲשֹׂתָהּ, and the rule מסייע אין בו ממש
overview: This עמוד finishes a ברייתא about two people carrying a heavy object out to רשות הרבים. רבי יהודה says they are liable if neither could carry it alone. רבי שמעון says they are always exempt, based on the word בַּעֲשֹׂתָהּ. The גמרא explains that the dispute depends on how many מיעוטים (exclusions) each one finds in the פסוק of the קרבן חטאת, and what each exclusion is used for. רבי יהודה uses one exclusion for a person who sinned by following a mistaken הוראת בית דין, while רבי מאיר counts only two exclusions. Next the גמרא asks who is liable when one person could do the act alone and the other could not. רב חסדא says it is the capable one, because מסייע אין בו ממש: help given to someone who could do it alone does not count. רב זביד proves this from a משנה about garments under an animal's legs. A rejection of that proof fails, so the proof stands. רב פפי then begins a second proof, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Two people carry a heavy object: רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with heavy objects, such as a round cake of pressed figs or a wooden beam, carried out by two people. רבי יהודה rules that they are liable if one person could not carry it alone, and exempt if one person could.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two people carried a round cake of pressed figs out to the public domain, or a beam out to the public domain: רבי יהודה says, if one person could not carry it out alone and two carried it out, they are liable. If not (one person could have done it alone), they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes two people carrying something too heavy for one person. רבי יהודה gives his ruling on that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's test is whether one person could have done the job alone. If neither could, then working together is the only normal way to do it, so both are liable. 'If not' means each of them could have done it alone; then the joint act is not a real מלאכה for them, so they are exempt. The mixed case, where one could and one could not, is discussed later in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: A round cake of pressed dried figs, which is heavy
A wooden beam
The public domain
Liable / exempt

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here means exempt from bringing a קרבן חטאת. It does not mean the act is permitted on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעִיגּוּל שֶׁל דְּבֵילָה וְהוֹצִיאוּהוּ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: With a round cake of figs, and they carried it out to the public domain,
with a beam, and they carried it out to the public domain,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
If one person could not carry it out alone
and two carried it out, they are liable;
and if not, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם לֹא יָכוֹל אֶחָד לְהוֹצִיאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun on the previous עמוד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, two people are liable when neither could do the act alone, and exempt when one of them could.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: two people are always exempt, from בַּעֲשֹׂתָהּ
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that even when neither person could carry the object alone, two people are exempt. He bases this on the word בַּעֲשֹׂתָהּ: an individual who does the act is liable, two who do it are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: even if one person could not carry it out alone, and two carried it out, they are exempt. That is why the Torah says 'בַּעֲשֹׂתָהּ' (when he does it): an individual who does it is liable, two who do it together are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה and exempts two people in every case. He gives a source from the Torah for his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון the number of people decides the law, not how heavy the object is. The word בַּעֲשֹׂתָהּ ('his doing it') shows that a חטאת applies only when one person does the whole act. Two people sharing the act are never liable.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When he does it' (ויקרא ד:כז), the source for רבי שמעון's exemption
An individual who did it alone
This is why it is stated

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל אֶחָד לְהוֹצִיאוֹ
phrases.english: Even if one person could not carry it out alone
and two carried it out, they are exempt.
For this it is stated: 'by doing it':
an individual who did it is liable;
two who did it are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא יָכוֹל אֶחָד לְהוֹצִיאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people who do one מלאכה together are always exempt, based on בַּעֲשֹׂתָהּ.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון actually depends on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it asks for the source behind the dispute so it can explain it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון cited בַּעֲשֹׂתָהּ, but רבי יהודה surely knows that word too. The גמרא wants to know how each one reads the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute in steps 1-2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reading of the פסוק separates רבי יהודה from רבי שמעון

steps.title: רבי שמעון finds three exclusions in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is about the פסוק of the חטאת of an individual. רבי שמעון reads three מיעוטים in it: one excludes one person lifting and another placing, one excludes two who could each do it alone, and one excludes two who could not do it alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about this פסוק: 'And if one person of the common people sins unintentionally, by doing it.' רבי שמעון holds that three exclusions are written: 'a person sins', 'one sins', 'by doing it sins'. One excludes a case where this one lifts and that one places. One excludes a case where this one could do it alone and that one could do it alone. One excludes a case where neither could do it alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the dispute is about how many exclusions the פסוק contains and what each one is for. It begins with רבי שמעון's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has three extra words: נֶפֶשׁ, אַחַת and בַּעֲשֹׂתָהּ. Each one limits the חטאת to a single person, and each covers a different kind of joint act. רבי שמעון uses the third one to exempt the 'neither could do it alone' case, which is exactly where he argues with רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Exclusions: words that limit a law
One person lifts the object and the other puts it down
Each person could have done it alone

keyTerms.term: זֶה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל וְזֶה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל
keyTerms.meaning: Neither person could have done it alone
Unintentionally

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a joint act can be split up in different ways. Each way needs its own exclusion from the Torah.

phrases.english: Over this verse:
'And if one person sins unintentionally
of the common people, by doing it.'
Rabbi Shimon holds:
three exclusions are written:
'a person sins', 'one sins', 'by doing it sins':

phrases.aramaic: חַד לְמַעוֹטֵי זֶה עוֹקֵר וְזֶה מַנִּיחַ,
phrases.english: one to exclude where this one lifts and that one places,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְמַעוֹטֵי זֶה יָכוֹל וְזֶה יָכוֹל,
phrases.english: and one to exclude where this one is able and that one is able,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְמַעוֹטֵי זֶה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל וְזֶה אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל.
phrases.english: and one to exclude where this one is unable and that one is unable.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about the מיעוטים in ויקרא ד:כז. רבי שמעון uses all three to exempt different kinds of joint acts.

steps.title: רבי יהודה uses the third exclusion differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה agrees with the first two exclusions. He uses the third for a different law: an individual who sinned by following a ruling of the בית דין is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה holds: one excludes where this one lifts and that one places; one excludes where this one could do it alone and that one could do it alone; and one excludes an individual who did it based on a ruling of the בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה does not exempt the 'neither could do it alone' case: he needs the third exclusion for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים count three exclusions. The difference is only in the third one. רבי יהודה uses it to exempt someone who acted on the בית דין's mistaken ruling, so no word is left to exempt two people who could not do it alone, and they stay liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A (mistaken) ruling issued by the court
One comes to exclude

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: חַד לְמַעוֹטֵי זֶה עוֹקֵר וְזֶה מַנִּיחַ,
phrases.english: one to exclude where this one lifts and that one places,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְמַעוֹטֵי זֶה יָכוֹל וְזֶה יָכוֹל,
phrases.english: and one to exclude where this one is able and that one is able,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְמַעוֹטֵי יָחִיד שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ בְּהוֹרָאַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and one to exclude an individual who did it by the ruling of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: חַד לְמַעוֹטֵי זֶה עוֹקֵר וְזֶה מַנִּיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's side of the answer to step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה uses the third מיעוט for הוראת בית דין, so two people who could not do it alone remain liable.

steps.title: רבי שמעון holds that one who follows the בית דין is liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי שמעון does not need a מיעוט for הוראת בית דין, because in his view an individual who acted on the בית דין's ruling is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds: an individual who did it based on a ruling of the בית דין is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes a gap: it explains why רבי שמעון does not use an exclusion for the הוראת בית דין case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, someone who sinned by following the court's mistake is still treated as an ordinary שוגג and brings a חטאת. Since he has no need to exempt that case, his third מיעוט is free for 'neither could do it alone'.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable (here, to bring a חטאת)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon:

phrases.aramaic: יָחִיד שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ בְּהוֹרָאַת בֵּית דִּין — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: an individual who did it by the ruling of the court is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: יָחִיד שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ בְּהוֹרָאַת בֵּית דִּין — חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון does not share רבי יהודה's use of the third מיעוט
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון holds that one who acts on a הוראת בית דין is liable, so he needs no exclusion for that case.

steps.title: How does רבי מאיר read the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי מאיר, who holds that two people who could each do it alone are liable. How does he deal with the exclusions?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it asks how רבי מאיר handles the extra words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes even 'each could do it alone' liable. If there were three exclusions, one should exempt that case. So how does he read the פסוק?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the analysis to a third תנא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי מאיר uses the מיעוטים, given that he makes זה יכול וזה יכול liable

steps.title: רבי מאיר counts only two exclusions
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads 'נפש אחת' as one phrase, so the פסוק has only two exclusions. He uses them for 'one lifts and the other places' and for הוראת בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written 'a person sins', 'one sins', 'by doing it sins'? Only two exclusions are written. One excludes where this one lifts and that one places, and one excludes an individual who did it based on a ruling of the בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר does not see three separate exclusions, only two. Neither of them is used for two people who could each do it alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'is it written...?' means: the words do not really split into three. 'נפש אחת' is one unit. With only two exclusions, רבי מאיר has none left for the 'each could do it alone' case, so in that case both are liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written? (a rhetorical question meaning 'it is not written so')
Two exclusions

steps.whatToRemember: Each extra word in the פסוק exempts one case. רבי שמעון: three words, all used for joint acts, so two people are always exempt. רבי יהודה: three words, one used for הוראת בית דין, so two who could not do it alone are liable. רבי מאיר: only two words, so even two who could each do it alone are liable.

phrases.english: Is it written
'a person sins', 'one sins', 'by doing it sins'?
Two exclusions are written:

phrases.aramaic: חַד לְמַעוֹטֵי זֶה עוֹקֵר וְזֶה מַנִּיחַ,
phrases.english: one to exclude where this one lifts and that one places,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד לְמַעוֹטֵי יָחִיד שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ בְּהוֹרָאַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and one to exclude an individual who did it by the ruling of the court.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר counts only two מיעוטים, one for זה עוקר וזה מניח and one for הוראת בית דין, so זה יכול וזה יכול remains liable.

steps.title: Which person is liable when only one could do it alone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier ruling that when one can and one cannot, all agree there is liability. It asks which of the two is the one who is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If this one is able and this one is not able, all agree he is liable. Which of them is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the earlier ברייתא and asks a clarifying question about it. It wants to know which of the two people is the liable one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'he is liable' without saying who. There are two people involved, so the גמרא needs to know whether the strong one, the weak one, or both are liable.

keyTerms.meaning: This one is able to do it alone and this one is not
Which of them?

phrases.english: The Master said:
This one is able and this one is not able:
everyone agrees he is liable.
Which of them is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier ברייתא after the discussion of the מיעוטים and asks about a case all agree on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In the case where one can and one cannot do it alone, who carries the liability?

steps.title: רב חסדא: the capable one is liable
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the one who could do it alone is liable, because the weak one is not really doing anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The one who is able. For if you say the one who is not able, what is he doing?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question: the capable person is the liable one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weak person could not have done the act alone, so his effort is not what got the job done. The strong person did the real work, so the liability falls on him.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he doing? Meaning he is not really doing anything

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The one who is able,
for if it were the one who is not able,
what is he doing!

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The capable person is liable; the incapable one contributes nothing that counts.

steps.title: רב המנונא: but the weak one is helping
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא objects that the weak person is doing something: he is helping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said to him: But he is helping him!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא challenges רב חסדא's reason. He says the weak one is not doing nothing, because he is helping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's reason was that the weak one does nothing. רב המנונא points out that the weak one does add real effort, so maybe he should share the liability.

keyTerms.meaning: He is helping him

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said to him:
But he is helping him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא: דְּקָא מְסַיַּיע בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the incapable person is doing nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Helping is a real action, so the weak person is contributing.

steps.title: Helping does not count
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that a helper's help has no legal weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A helper has no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends himself with a short rule: help given to someone who could do it alone counts for nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא agrees the weak one is physically helping. He says that in הלכה, help like this is not an act of its own, so it cannot make the helper liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A helper has no substance: help does not count legally

steps.whatToRemember: The key rule of this סוגיא is 'מסייע אין בו ממש': help given to someone who could do it alone does not count.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A helper has no substance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מְסַיֵּיעַ אֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the legal value of the action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Helping is real participation and should create liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: Help to someone who could act alone has no legal weight.

steps.title: Proof from garments under an animal's legs
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד in the name of רבא brings a משנה: garments under a bed's four legs become impure from a זב, but garments under an animal's four legs stay pure. This seems to show that a helping leg does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said in the name of רבא: We also learned this. If a זב was sitting on a bed and four garments were under the bed's legs, they are impure, because a bed cannot stand on three. And רבי שמעון says pure. If he was riding on an animal and four garments were under the animal's legs, they are pure, because it can stand on three. But why? The legs are helping each other! Is it not because we say a helper has no substance?
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד brings a proof from a משנה about טומאה for the rule that help does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bed needs all four legs, so each leg really carries the זב, and the garments are impure. An animal can stand on three legs, so each leg is only a 'helper'. The garments stay pure, which fits the rule that a helper does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it: a formula for bringing support from a משנה
A man with a certain discharge who makes things impure by lying or sitting on them
Garments or cloths
Impure / pure

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'וְאַמַּאי' is asked on the חכמים, who say the garments under the bed are impure. Even they agree the garments under the animal are pure, and the גמרא wants to know why.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava:
We too have also learned it:
If he (a זב) was sitting on a bed,
and four garments were under the legs of the bed,

phrases.aramaic: — טְמֵאוֹת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד עַל שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: they are impure, because it cannot stand on three legs,
and Rabbi Shimon rules them pure.
If he was riding on an animal,
and four garments were under the legs of the animal,

phrases.aramaic: — טְהוֹרוֹת, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיְּכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד עַל שָׁלֹשׁ.
phrases.english: they are pure, because it can stand on three legs.
But why? The legs are helping one another!

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן מְסַיֵּיעַ אֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ?
phrases.english: Is it not because we say a helper has no substance?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a משנה for רב חסדא's rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of garments under the legs of a bed versus an animal carrying a זב.

steps.title: Maybe the animal fully lifted a leg
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא says help may count after all. The garments are pure because the animal fully lifts one leg at a time, so that leg is not helping at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה of Diskarta said: Really, I can tell you that a helper does have substance. It is different here, because the animal lifts its leg completely.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא pushes away רב זביד's proof by giving another reason the garments are pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says the animal's case is not about a helping leg. An animal actually picks up one leg fully, so at that moment that leg carries nothing. So the משנה proves nothing about help.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you: a formula for keeping the opposite view
A helper does have substance
It lifted its leg completely

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda of Diskarta said:
Really, I can tell you
that a helper has substance,
and here it is different,
because it lifts its leg completely.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ מְסַיֵּיעַ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רב חסדא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The animal's case may be about a leg that is fully lifted, not a leg that is helping.

steps.title: Switching legs is like a זב who rolls over
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב יהודה's idea. The animal lifts different legs at different times. Whenever one leg is up, each of the other three is truly needed to hold the animal. So every leg, at some point, really carries the זב. That is like a זב who rolls onto each bench, and all the garments should be impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since sometimes it lifts this leg and sometimes that one, it should be like a זב who turns over! Did we not learn: A זב lying on five benches or five money belts: lengthwise, they are impure; widthwise, they are pure. If he slept, and he may have turned over on them, they are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה מדיסקרתא's answer by comparing it to a משנה about a זב who rolls over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On רב יהודה's reading, a leg that is down while another is lifted is a real carrier, not a helper. Since the animal lifts each leg in turn, every leg is a real carrier at some moment. A זב who shifts his weight from place to place makes every place impure. So on רב יהודה's reading all four garments should be impure, but the משנה says they are pure.

Benches

Along their length / across their width

phrases.english: A זב who was lying on five benches
or on five money belts:
if along their length, they are impure;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דְּזִימְנִין עָקְרָה הָא, וְזִימְנִין עָקְרָה הָא, לֶיהֱוֵי כְּזָב הַמִּתְהַפֵּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא's claim that the garments are pure because a leg is fully lifted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lifting legs in turn means each leg is, at some point, an essential support rather than a helper, like a זב rolling over, which would make all the garments impure.

steps.title: The proof stands: help does not count
steps.stepSummary: Since the lifted-leg answer fails, the only reason left is that a helping leg does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not because we say a helper has no substance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רב זביד's proof is back in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lifted-leg answer would make the garments impure, but the משנה says pure. So the only explanation left is that each leg is just a helper, and help does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not: brings the גמרא back to the earlier proof

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about garments under an animal stands as a proof for רב חסדא: מסייע אין בו ממש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes from step 15 that the proof of step 13 returns.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The animal-garments משנה proves מסייע אין בו ממש.

steps.title: רב פפי begins a second proof
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי in the name of רבא announces that he also has a proof from a משנה. The proof itself comes on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: We too have also learned it,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב פפי announces a second proof for the same rule, and the source itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is adding more support for 'מסייע אין בו ממש'. No new content is given yet; only the start of the proof appears here.
